 N.Y. Democrats rally in Brooklyn night before Election Day
 BY 
 Bernadette Hogan
 New York City 
 PUBLISHED 10:43 PM ET Nov. 02, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 10:43 PM EST Nov. 02, 2026 
 SHARE 
 New York Democrats looked to keep the energy up before Election Day at a rally in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, Monday. 
 Gov. Kathy Hochul aims to run up the score among five borough voters. 
 "We don't allow here in New York state, [Donald] Trump-style leadership which is what Bruce Blakeman said he would bring to New York," Hochul said during a party rally at Brooklyn Bowl.
 "I'm not making this up, you'd think he'd have pollsters who told him not to do that. And just today, JD Vance was in New York state saying some nasty things about our candidates — but you know what? We're going to be the ones left standing. We're going to leave you in the dust," she continued. 
 Hochul is also focused on the Empire State's possible contribution toward flipping congressional control.
 Rep. Hakeem Jeffries turning ire toward the GOP and President Donald Trump — in his own bid to become the next, and first African American, speaker of the House. 
 "So we've made clear as Democrats all across the country that if you got folks out there stealing from the American people, shortchanging the American people or screwing over the American people," the House Minority Leader said, slamming Republicans.
 "Beginning on Day one of Congress, we're going to hold the crooks accountable. We're going to hold you accountable," he added.
 The polls open Election Day at 6 a.m. and close at 9 p.m.
